title: Introduction to Linear Algebra
body: Linear algebra studies vectors, matrices and linear transformations. Eigenvalues and eigenvectors describe how a matrix stretches space.

title: Understanding C++ Memory Management
body: In C++ objects can live on the stack or the heap. Smart pointers such as unique_ptr and shared_ptr manage heap memory automatically and prevent leaks.

title: Structs versus Classes in C++
body: A struct and a class differ only in default access: struct members are public, class members are private. Classes usually bundle data with behaviour.

title: The French Revolution
body: The French Revolution began in 1789 with the storming of the Bastille and transformed France from a monarchy into a republic.

title: Photosynthesis Explained
body: Plants convert sunlight, water and carbon dioxide into glucose and oxygen inside chloroplasts through photosynthesis.

title: How Search Engines Work
body: A search engine crawls documents, builds an inverted index mapping words to documents, and ranks results with scores such as TF-IDF.

title: The Printing Press
body: Johannes Gutenberg introduced movable type printing around 1440, which spread books and literacy across Europe.

title: Statistics: Mean, Median and Mode
body: The mean is the average, the median is the middle value and the mode is the most frequent value. Standard deviation measures spread.

title: Sorting Algorithms Compared
body: Quicksort and mergesort run in O(n log n) on average. Insertion sort is O(n^2) but fast on small or nearly sorted arrays.

title: The Apollo 11 Moon Landing
body: On 20 July 1969 Apollo 11 landed on the Moon and Neil Armstrong became the first person to walk on its surface.

title: Black Holes
body: A black hole is a region of space where gravity is so strong that nothing, not even light, can escape beyond the event horizon.

title: Hash Tables in Practice
body: A hash table maps keys to buckets using a hash function, giving average constant time lookup. Collisions are resolved by chaining or probing.
